A good comparison is those cables are much like an old car - it should get you there, whereas this cable is like a high end sports car - it will get you there lightning fast, without failure.

This Cat8 is typically thicker than other grades of Ethernet cable due to the extra shielding within and additional insulation.

What makes this cable really exceptional are the connector ports. Not only are the ports reinforced at each end of the wire, which really help hold all of the wires in place even if you have to bend and twist it to fit it within the plug - they are hinged helping prevent tension damage to the port.

This Cat8 Ethernet Cable I got is 3’ long which made it ideal for using to directly connect my NAS into my router . This is a critical connection for my system - while I have tested several cables none have worked better.

You will not find a better Cat8 Ethernet Cable - this is really a top of the line cable that is easy to work with and is made to hold up long term.

This is a purchase that you’ll never regret.

text_fidelity_a:
Western Digital 3TB WD Purple Surveillance Internal Hard Drive HDD - SATA 6 Gb/s, 64 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD30PURZ I purchased this as a data storage/backup drive for my desktop PC. My main drive is a1TB NVME drive. The data drive I use for movies, songs, and backups and digital images. Since I am not booting with the drive I don't care about raw performance, nor will I pay for it. With that said I am VERY happy with this drive. It only spins at 5400 RPM, so the access time is slightly slower, but it makes no difference to me. Maximum transfer rate is nearly 200MB/sec. High capacity drives have dense platters and are able to pull data faster.

I am a Nazi for eliminating extraneous sound and used to keep my drives inside enclosures to reduce sound. My quietest drive to date is the Samsung HD 503HI, and this is even quieter. I have several large case fans spinning slowly and if I turn them off I can ever so slightly hear a faint humming or click, but otherwise I hear NOTHING.

This is my first WD drive (have always used Samsung). I cannot speak to the drive's reliability as I've only had it for one month. It is labeled for "Surveillance," so if it's meant to be running 24/7- 365 it is meant to get use in commercial/industrial environments.

I think everyone with a desktop PC should adopt this system. It is very easy to backup anything important- save it to your C: drive as well as your backup E: drive or whatever. If one your main drive goes kaput you have the backup to pull your saved data from. You can use flash drives for additional redundancy and portability, but in my experience they are not so reliable.
text_fidelity_b: Western Digital 3TB WD Purple Surveillance Internal Hard Drive HDD - SATA 6 Gb/s, 64 MB Cache, 3.5" - WD30PURZ

text_fidelity_a:
HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed) I wanted to wait and use it a while before leaving a review.

First off, it is larger than I expected it to be. That's okay - just had to rearrange everything.
Secondly, it is a refurb, so there are limits as to what to expect. My old computer had a hard drive die.
I got a new hard drive, but for some reason, it would never connect to the internet again after that.
I downloaded new drivers, etc etc, but nothing. So, couldn't really go without any longer, so looked for a refurb.

I like sticking with HP because I've used them for years. I've even had refurbs.
This one is different.
First of all, it lays horizontally instead of like the towers I've always had.
It looks a little rough, but not unreasonable.

it grunts at me while using it, much like my old dying hard drive did, so that does worry me a little bit.
It sounds like a grumpy old man who doesn't want to get out of his chair to reach the remote.
There are plenty of USB ports on this one. It lacks some things I'd like to have, but hey...

My biggest complaint is the lack of RAM memory on this. It only came with a measly 8GB.
That might sound okay, but it isn't. Everything moves in slow-motion. Copying files is a nightmare.
I can't afford to buy more memory right now, so I have to just suck it up.
We raided a couple of my other computers which are all HP, but of course, NONE of the six memory sticks I had
will fit this one. *bang head on desk*
The speakers are HORRIBLE. If you have ears, you'll want to replace them or add your own.
I do have speakers, but have not yet hooked them up, because it has to be done on the back, and I have to move
a lot of stuff to pull it back out enough.

This also has Win10, which I dislike a great deal. Seems like everything was moved to a new place just because they could.
But I'll deal with that. Most of the time, I can ignore the Win10 junk.

Overall, it will do what I hired it for, which was to get me back on the internet.
But if you work with graphics (like I do), know that the lack of memory will be sand in your shorts.
Everything takes much longer than on my old HP tower.
text_fidelity_b: HP 8100 Desktop Computer Intel i5 3.2GHz Processor 8GB Memory 1TB HDD Genuine Windows 10 Professional (Renewed)

TPone Bluetooth Speakers, Outdoor Portable Wireless Speaker with Subwoofer, IPX6 Waterproof, 80w (Peak) Loud Stereo Sound, Deep Bass with Rhythm Lights for Home Party Beach Camping I like listening to music when I spend time in my backyard. I used to rely on my alexa for this purpose, but more often than not, the volume and clarity were not that good. A portable Bluetooth speaker was the answer and I found just what I needed with this Bluetooth, from Tpone.

What you get with this Bluetooth is a portable, chargeable speaker with that offers up to 18 hours of playback on a single charge. Getting it fully charged will take time, but after that, it’s a matter of pairing it with the Bluetooth on your phone. In about two minutes, it will be ready for use.

The sound quality you get with this Bluetooth speaker is quite good. I like the bass, and for my needs, the volume is sufficient. It’s not powerful enough to blast you away, but for what I need, the volume level works. I use it mostly when I sit on my back patio and/or jump in the pool. I don’t need extreme volume, so this works. There is a plus and minus button on the unit that at first seem like volume controls, but they are not. If you push these, the music will either advance forward or backward to the next song on the list. The volume is controlled by your phone or whatever device you have paired.

There are different colored lights on this speaker that react to the music, adding to the visuals. Again, for my needs, I really don’t care about the lights. But I can see how this could certainly add to the coolness factor for some people. The added colors and the way they react to the intensity of the music is a nice addition. Oh, and I like that I can use this to charge my phone. If a phone is paired, it could drain the phone’s power quickly while you play music. You can easily counter this by plugging your phone directly into the unit, helping to keep your phone charged.

Having the means to listen to music is an ongoing need for me. Whether I am listening to music in my backyard or taking a trip to a nearby beach, I need to be able to play my tunes and the easiest way is to use a portable Bluetooth speaker. This Bluetooth from Tpone delivers on most all counts. The easy pairing, the bass, and the overall sound quality make this an easy winner and an excellent Bluetooth choice.
text_fidelity_b: TPone Bluetooth Speakers, Outdoor Portable Wireless Speaker with Subwoofer, IPX6 Waterproof, 80w (Peak) Loud Stereo Sound, Deep Bass with Rhythm Lights for Home Party Beach Camping

text_fidelity_a:
Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector I was actually really shocked at how great this little portable speaker is. My cell phone found it in seconds, and in less than a minute I was listening to music from my cell phone, only out of this little speaker, it actually sounded great. In fact, the bass was so effective out of this thing that some of my favorite songs made it dance around the table.

I love that it is so much louder than the music I get out of my cell phone, and I also love that I can listen to hip-hop and rap and enjoy actual bass, which usually doesn't come through for my cell phone speaker at all.

You can actually control the music from your cell phone from the speaker itself. It has a pause/play button, forward and back, and volume controls. It also has a speakerphone control, in case you wanted to have a quick conversation from the speaker itself. I would not personally want to use the speaker as a speakerphone, but it is nice to have the option in a pinch.

The one thing I didn't care for is that when you tap the volume button and it hits its maximum, it beeps at you to let you know that it won't go any louder. It's a pretty annoying sound, and in my view they could just have left that feature out. I'm sure I would figure it out soon enough that it wouldn't go any louder.

Overall, I was really surprised at the quality, ease of setup, and range of sound from this cute little speaker. I'm delighted to own it, and anticipate it getting a lot of use over the coming months and years.
text_fidelity_b: Portable Pocket WOWOTO Projector Android Mini Smart LED DLP Projector

eBoot 100 Pieces Adhesive Cable Clips Wire Clips Cable Wire Management Wire Cable Holder Clamps Cable Tie Holder for Car, Office and Home I traded my Jeep in for a GMC 2500HD pickup truck. I kept my radar detector and dash camera. I bought these clips to run the wiring around the windshield with.

These clips are exactly the same as the OEM clips that came with the dash camera. They are well designed and well made. The clip has two ways to run the wires. One way is to just lay the wire in the clip and snap it shut. The other way is through a split-ring, built into the clip. I was able to run three wires (radar detector, dash camera power and rear camera lead) through the clips and they are still securely fastened.

The 3M tape on the clips holds very well. However, you will need to do what you can to prevent the cabin from getting too hot. Extreme temps will cause them to loosen and fall off. Here in central Texas, it gets really hot in the summer. I use a windshield sun guard to keep the cabin a little cooler. I also installed some AVS window vent shades. I'm able to leave the windows cracked just a little. This also helps to keep the cabin a little cooler.

This very economical pack of 100 will help a lot. I have two more vehicles to tidy up. This is a great product at a very low price. Five stars.
text_fidelity_b: eBoot 100 Pieces Adhesive Cable Clips Wire Clips Cable Wire Management Wire Cable Holder Clamps Cable Tie Holder for Car, Office and Home

LeadsaiL Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 4 Buttons, AA Battery Used, USB Mouse for Laptop, Desktop, MacBook Great shape, very much like the classic and ubiquitous Logitech. I like that the pairing device is on-board. Lightweight and simple, a mouse is important for me if needing to get serious work done, especially anything with CAD or Visio.

The big question you need to ask yourself is, do you want a Bluetooth version or one like this that has its own receiver. It seems to me that if you always use this with the same computer and you have Bluetooth built in to the computer, then you probably want Bluetooth. Conversely, if you want this to use with multiple computers and/or you don't have Bluetooth built in to any one of the computers you will use the mouse with, then you'd want something like this. This is because pairing is easier in a case such as this, and drivers usually aren't an issue. Bluetooth usually isn't an issue either, but it might get irritating with frequent changing of machines. At least that is my experience.

Does not come with a carry bag, surprisingly. Mouse roller also functions as a button, as it should. It has an on/off switch on the back, which is nice for saving battery life and being able to leave this hooked up to a permanent install (although with a permanent desk setup, I personally stick with wired).
text_fidelity_b: LeadsaiL Wireless Computer Mouse, 2.4G Portable Slim Cordless Mouse Less Noise for Laptop Optical Mouse with 4 Buttons, AA Battery Used, USB Mouse for Laptop, Desktop, MacBook

Avantree Oasis B Bluetooth 5.0 Transmitter Receiver for TV, Home Stereo Speakers, Bypass Mode, Class 1 Long Range, LED Indicator, Optical AUX RCA, aptX Low Latency Audio Adapter for 2 Headphones I had previously owned another Bluetooth transmitter by Avantree, which cost very little less than this one, but the caliber of this transmitter is massively better than the old one. So they must have made some useful advances in the relevant technology in the four years since I last purchased a transmitter from them.

I have tested this transmitter with multiple Bluetooth headphones that I own, and in each case, the Bluetooth connects seamlessly. I like the fact that the transmitter speaks and lets me know when the Bluetooth has connected. And a split second after that, the sound from my TV comes through my Bluetooth headphones. My old Avantree transmitter had neither of those abilities. It would take up to 2 minutes to get it connected to my Bluetooth headphones after multiple tries, and the sound's clarity and volume weren't nearly as good.

As was the case with my previous transmitter, this one can handle multiple Bluetooth headphones at the same time. So far I have only attempted transmission with two at a time.

Finally, the appearance of this transmitter is much fancier than the old one. I will admit that it is about three times larger than the old one, but that is not really a problem for me, because the old one was tiny and this one is still conveniently small. It has some cute, space-age looking little antennas on it that the other one didn't have, which may partially account for why it works so much better.

All in all, I am very pleased with this purchase.
text_fidelity_b: Avantree Oasis B Bluetooth 5.0 Transmitter Receiver for TV, Home Stereo Speakers, Bypass Mode, Class 1 Long Range, LED Indicator, Optical AUX RCA, aptX Low Latency Audio Adapter for 2 Headphones

The photos can be shared immediately, and I don't have to remove the card from my camera to transfer the photos to a PC or mobile device. (The Eye-Fi cards can also be read directly from a photo card reader or from a PC card reader slot.)

This Eye-Fi Mobi Pro card is much, much faster than my "legacy" Eye-Fi card. The Mobi Pro works just like the older card in my Panasonic Lumix DMC-LX2S camera. (The Eye-Fi web site has a long, long list of compatible cameras you can check before buying any Eye-Fi card.)

Uploads to the Eye-Fi Cloud seem almost instantaneous, and the transfers to my PC take about a quarter of the time required by the older card. The wireless transmissions do tend to drain my camera battery though. You'll need to recharge frequently or keep extra batteries on hand.

The Eye-Fi Mobi Pro app transfers your photos and videos directly into "Eye-Fi Pictures", "Eye-Fi RAW", and "Eye-Fi Videos" folders on your PC. The software's default setting groups the transferred files into subfolders of these folders by date.

The Mobi Pro app also uploads your photos to the Eye-Fi Cloud and groups them by date. In the Eye-Fi Cloud you can do simple editing (rotate, crop), add captions, and create albums. You get a one-year free subscription to the Eye-Fi Cloud with each Mobi Pro card; renewals are $4.99 a month, or $49.99 a year. The Eye-Fi Cloud is a convenience, but your Mobi Pro card will continue to be completely functional if you decide that you don't need the Eye-Fi Cloud storage. You can upload to the Eye-Fi Cloud from anywhere, not just from your home network.

You get the Mobi Pro app/software by going to the web address printed on the box (just below the space for the included card reader). The software is clean and simple, with settings for uploading and downloading photos--automatically or manually--to either the Eye-Fi Cloud, your PC, or both.

I always have to fuss for a while to get any Eye-Fi software set up properly. (Tip: Don't try to set up the Eye-Fi Mobi app on two PCs at once, with both PCs turned on. This confuses the software, and also the wireless connections. I had to uninstall the software from one PC, and recycle my router because my PC lost the ability to communicate with the router. The price I paid for stupidity!)

Ever since I got my first Eye-Fi card, I haven't wanted to use anything else in my camera. This Eye-Fi Mobi Pro card is tremendously advanced over that first card, in both speed and versatility, and I love it even more.
text_fidelity_b: Eyefi mobiProZ-32 Mobi Pro 32GB WiFi SDHC CARD with One Year Eyefi Cloud

The problem as many have stated is most commercial WiFi system require you log into a splash page after you connect to their network. This router does not have a way to do that. You can try using one of your devices and then clone the MAC address to the router, but this only works if this router is connected to the network with the Ethernet cable port. Most hotels and hospitals no longer have working Ethernet jacks in rooms. If you try and clone the MAC address on the wireless port it creates a conflict and everything stops working.

So to sum up, it works fine as a cheap travel router, but if you have to deal with a splash page on an WiFi only network, it simply will not work. It can’t be that hard to create one of these with a built in browser for splash pages. Anyone listening????

Philips SHE9850 in-Ear Headphones with Advanced Acoustics (Discontinued by Manufacturer) These are perhaps the best in ear earphones I've ever used. They are lightweight, comfortable, stay in your ear, and offer great sound.

I've long ago ditched most earbud style earphones. They offer horrible sound, are uncomfortable, and never stay in your ear. These earphones address those issues with style, comfort, and great sound reproduction.

The mid and high range reproduction is crisp and clean without any noticeable distortion. Low range is somewhat lacking but is proberly above what most small earbud style headphones are.

They feature many great design features such as replaceable buds for the earpiece. There is small, medium, and large. There is also a set of memory foam that you can choose. This is good because as everyone's ears are different, most earpieces are not. This allows you to choose the fit of the earbuds to suit your own needs.

The part of the cable that plugs into your walkman, diskman, iPod or whatever is steel reinforced, which is nice as that is what usually breaks first on headphones. They also come with a steel carrying case to protect your headphones when not in use. They also have a cleaning tool to clean any nasty bits that may get into the canal of the phones.

All-in-all a great set of phones for the audiophile. They are lightweight, sound great, and most importantly, stay in your ear and are comfortable.

Tripod

text_fidelity_a:
Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model) I purchased this at the end of July 2014 along with:

[[ASIN:B00E5NOXM4 Google Nexus 7 2013 Case - Poetic Google Nexus 7 2013 Case [Slimline Series] - [Lightweight] [Ultra-slim] PU Leather Slim-Fit Trifold Cover Stand Folio Case for Google Nexus 7 2nd Gen 2013 Black (3 Year Manufacturer Warranty From Poetic)]]

[[ASIN:B008MOHLVC Stylus, amPen® Hybrid Stylus (Black) for Apple iPad Air/iPad 2/iPad Mini, Apple iPhone 6 (4.7)/6 Plus (5.5)/5/5s/5c/4s, Nexus 5/7, Galaxy Tab 4/3/2, Galaxy S5/S4, HTC One M8/M7 (Interchangeable Hybrid Tip Feature)]].

I also ordered the [[ASIN:1937842282 Google Nexus 7 (Android 4.4 KitKat Edition)]] book as a compliment to this purchase.

I waited almost six months to write this review because I wanted to "cool off" from my installation experience that would have caused me to rate this 3 stars. I am also now able to fairly assess this tablet after a few months' use.

I wanted a highly-rated unrestricted (open) tablet that provided great graphics and sufficient screen space. I purchased this to use on a Wi-Fi network only for when I didn't want to boot up my laptop to check mail or see a movie, etc. I also did not want an Apple tablet because my boyfriend has an iPad 3 and the Apple products have restrictions. I also was not impressed with the graphics on his iPad. I was considering a Kindle Fire HD 7" but that tablet was too restrictive as well and was geared to Amazon junkies. I am an Amazon junkie but I also do not like restrictions on products I purchase. During my July 2014 research, I discovered that the Nexus 7 tablet was the highest rated Android next to those more restrictive tablets.

After I received the Nexus, I wondered if I had made the right decision. First, I was surprised that this came with no documentation (other than the business card sized diagram of where all the ports were and a warranty and safety agreement in both English and French). The documentation didn't even say how long I needed to charge the unit. I charged it overnight and then had immense trouble getting this connected.

The router I was connecting to has MAC filtering enabled so I needed the MAC address. However, I couldn't get the MAC address without setting up the device. Also, I couldn't set it up because I couldn't get the MAC address. I could have fussed with the router and turned off MAC filtering/security temporarily but I had to get to work in the morning right after the unit completed charging. I then tried connecting via three other networks (my library for one, my work another, and another Wi-Fi connection). It still would not connect. Because I didn't want to wait until I got home 12 hours later to fuss with my router I wound up asking a tech support person where I work. He connected me via his personal MiFi mobile hotspot.

Apparently, Google Nexus only connects to certain networks if the first time setup has not been done. I tried several open networks. My co-worker's MiFi mobile network connection, although I suspect mine would have connected had I temporarily removed the security on my router, was the only one that would allow me to run the automatic setup so that I could connect. After setup was performed, I was able to get the MAC address from the settings "about" tab. I was also able to connect to the three other networks I tried previously and after inputting the MAC address, I could also connect to my router. It was apparently the initial setup process that prevented the connection.

This Google Nexus would have gotten five stars if they enhanced the user experience by:
1 - Providing a MAC address either on the unit or on a piece of paper for those that have MAC filtering enabled.
2 - Providing a documentation pamphlet with the unit that:
* Tells the user how long they need to charge the unit the first time.
* Explains to the user that setup cannot be run on all networks and sometimes they will get an error message. Therefore, they might say something like "using your own network is advisable" or provide an explanation of why certain networks (including totally open ones that allow all connections) would not work. Perhaps there is some sort of technical protocol that is not available on all networks; I have no idea.

Other than the above, I absolutely love my Google Nexus. I've been using this for almost 6 months and it has met my every expectation. It charges in less than four hours; lasts about 3 hours if I'm constantly using it; lasts about 3-4 days when I'm using it for about 10 minutes daily. I've used this for email, movies, web surfing, pictures, etc. App availability is unending (Kindle, LinkedIn, Battery Doctor, etc., etc.) I tested the screen image next to my co-workers Kindle Fire HD 7" and there is no discernible difference in quality or resolution. Images and movies on this device are superb. If I attach my [[ASIN:B00N4SIIFY APLWL USB 2.0 A to Micro B Cable 6FT-TPE jacket-Blue]] to my laptop, I can both charge the unit and also access files on it from my laptop such as the photos located under Nexus 7\Internal storage\DCIM\Camera directory (that's Computer\Nexus 7\Internal storage\DCIM\Camera in Explorer).

Overall this is a quality tablet that did not disappoint me once I got past the initial installation and lack of documentation headache. In the comments section of my review, I put links to Google documentation I found helpful as well as to the 2014 review I used for my research.

UPDATE Jan 6, 2015 - Right after I wrote this review I had a problem where my Nexus was shutting down automatically and every time I went to use it I had to power it back up. After doing an Internet search I was able to fix this by going to the Play Store app on the Nexus, then selecting "My Apps" and accepting all install updates. There were a few updates that had not installed and this was playing havoc with my system. After I did this, the Nexus remained powered up and has been working fine the last several days.
text_fidelity_b: Asus Nexus 7 2B32 7-Inch 32 GB Tablet, Black (2013 Model)

Appearance:
Their product description calls this 'fun, trendy and modern'. But to be honest this looks, to me, like an appliance that fell out of my grandmother's 1950's black, white and chrome art-deco kitchen. It's not unpleasant looking but I wouldn't call it modern. When I saw images of the system online I had hopes that the neon green ring around the face would light up. Sadly it doesn't. The handle is also fixed in place and doesn't retract or collapse into the body. It would have been a nice idea so you could stack or store this more easily.

Sound:
It doesn't sound bad. Especially for being just two 15 watt wide range speakers in a ported (holes to help the bass sound better) enclosure. The bass is a little flat and the high end sounds a little... hollow but it is a lot better than the speakers built into my tablet. I've tried a variety of music; jazz, pop, classical, rock, punk and everything sounded quite good. I found I had to use both the tablet's volume control as well as the speaker systems volume controls to get real volume out of the system. They operate independently of each other.

Drawbacks:
I don't normally comment on price with items received from the Vine program but at the time I'm writing this review Amazon is currently selling this item for over two hundred dollars. Maybe the Bluetooth equipment is expensive but to me that's a LOT for just two speakers in a box. I didn't pay that much for my four speaker bookshelf system or the subwoofer equipped speaker system connected to my desktop PC. Both of which have far superior sound quality.

The battery indicator light only seems to light up when the system is charging. I charged this a week ago and used it for several hours at a time but I have no idea how much charge is left in the battery.

The biggest problem I had with this speaker system was when doing anything other than playing music. I thought it would be fun to add big sound to the games I enjoy on my tablet but there's a distinct lag between doing anything and when the speaker plays the sound. I noticed it most of all in my favorite billiards simulator. You would strike a ball...and then hear it happen, even system sounds such as keyboard typing noises, a 'blip' when selecting things played a noticeable time after they happened.

The App:
I won't say much about the app here. It's completely unnecessary to operate this system with your Android device. It's just poor quality programming that appears to have been slapped together at the last minute. It also doesn't match the documentation and features such as Bass Boost which are in the instructions but don't exist in the app.

Speaking of the documentation. I opened the box and found a large booklet and for one, brief, moment I thought this item was fully documented in depth and detail... then I opened the instructions and found there's twelve pages of English instructions which are poorly written and lacking in detail. The rest of the book is comprised of numerous other languages each getting their own few pages. Ah well. Turn it on, turn it up. Enjoy the music.
text_fidelity_b: Hercules Wireless Bluetooth Speaker (White/Green)

text_fidelity_a:
Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000 Not being a techie, this review will be based on the experiences of an average Joe or Jane trying this keyboard on for size.

Pros:

1. Excellent packaging. Easy to open, and is packed in a compact and attractive box. Would make a great gift.
2. Nice comfortable palm rest and key positioning. The removable feet required a bit of reading of the instructions to set up, but this was relatively easily accomplished. Note: Be careful you don't throw out the feet with the packaging.
3. Easy set up. Up and running in minutes.
4. Works with batteries, so no need to store and locate a charger when the mouse runs out of steam. (As compared to the Logitech model)
5. Handy buttons for MS Office, such as cut, copy, paste, undo, bold, italic and underline (et al) right on the keyboard. (as dual key functions)
6. Media keys and volume controls on keyboard, also low battery indicator light.
7. Compact footprint, so it can fit most workstations.

Cons:

1. Can you say "dust magnet"? This thing picks up dust and fingerprints like crazy, especially on the shiny bits.
2. Lack of detailed instructions for the keyboard and mouse. It comes with adequate set-up instructions, but expects you to know what to do after that. I'd have appreciated some included info on the keyboard functions.
3. No lights for Caps lock and Num lock
4. Mouse has no on/off switch (that I can find), so when I turned it over and put in the batteries (2 x AA included) I nearly blinded myself with the blue laser. Note: It turns off when the receiver is stored in the base.
5. Mouse is obese. Hard for small hands to deal with, and not ergonomic.

Note:
I don't have Windows 7 as yet, but it's nice to know that whenever I get it, the keyboard has special "hot keys" to allow easy access to programmes.

Overall, a good keyboard/mouse combination for the price, with more positive features than negative if you're an average computer user. I can't speak for Gamers or Techies, but I like it.

Amanda Richards, January 3, 2010
text_fidelity_b: Microsoft Wireless Comfort Desktop 5000

text_fidelity_a: Linksys LGS308MP Business Poe+ Smart 8 Port Gigabit Network Switch (130W),Black Pretty much a plug and play device; 1 minute to install.  There is supposed to be a configuration program that you can access, but I wasn't able to do so with the IP address given in the instructions.  It wasn't necessary anyway, as the device functions just fine on a simple network without any additional configuration.  There are two things I didn't like about it compared to my old switch, that I was replacing.  First of all, it is a bit larger than my old switch at 8 1/2 inches long compared to my old one that is only 6 1/2 inches.  Also, the power supply is considerably larger at 6 inches long and 3 inches wide and 1 inch thick.  My old switch uses only a large plug that is 1 3/4 x 1 3/4 x 1 1/4.  The second thing I didn't like is that there are no indicator lights to show the functioning ports.  My old switch has lights for each port that is working, which is nice.  You may prefer not to have any lights and if so, this Linksys switch may be to your liking.  Note: there is a disc included with documentation, but I didn't find it to be of any particular use.  On the plus side, this does appear to be a quality, heavy duty switch, so might be well suited for a commercial application (such as in an unattended area, like a computer room in a large business).  It appears to weigh nearly twice what my old switch did, so it is solid.  I have used Linksys products before and found them to be good quality with no issues.  You can buy a cheaper switch that is smaller and does essentially the same thing at a considerably lower price, but you most likely won't get the same quality as you would with this switch.  Also this switch does apparently have a POE (power over internet) feature and if you need that, you also might want to get this.  I don't see a need for POE in my configuration.  Possibly overkill for typical home office, but if you want a good quality switch, it might be worth the extra cost (or not).
text_fidelity_b: Linksys LGS308MP Business Poe+ Smart 8 Port Gigabit Network Switch (130W),Black

text_fidelity_a:
CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition This is a very complete kit and does contain everything you need to setup a Raspberry Pi 3. Yes, the op system installs easily and, with luck, you can be up and running in less than an hour. So, why the 2 stars?

It gets 2 stars because the Raspberry Pi is probably one of the most frustrating devices I've ever tried to put to any real use. For example, I wanted to set it up so I could use a VNC server on the Pi and a VNC client on my Mac (OS X El Capitan). After three days of almost non-stop failures, I'm sick of this thing. Researching how to get this task done leads you down a black hole of internet articles and posts on the Raspberry Pi site, most of that give different instructions, use different commands, tell you which files to edit and what to put in them, and almost none work, period!

The core problem rests squarely on the Raspberry Pi organization. Their own website is full of conflicting posts on how to do just about anything beyond a basic setup. Few, if any posts state which model of Pi is being referenced, and many bear no date. All in all, it's a very frustrating experience and, while I like to tinker with these things, a little success is required once in a while to keep me chugging along. I think I'm done with this thing. I had hoped it would finally be a Linux for the rest of us. Unfortunately, it's just as convoluted and difficult to use as any version of Linux out there (my opinion).

However, if you're looking to explore the Pi, this kit has everything you need to do a basic setup of Linux. And, should you want to use it as a web server, file server, media server, you're really on your own. Drink lots of coffee and plan to pull our lots of hair.
text_fidelity_b: CanaKit Raspberry Pi 3 Complete Starter Kit - 32 GB Edition

I tried it with both my 2017 15" Intel MB Pro and the redesigned 2020 16" MB Pro with a thicker bottom case.

I tend to lean my hands on the edge of my laptop, so I found the rise on the edge to be somewhat high when using it with my older computer, although I do appreciate having the extra fans for cooling on that model because Intel Mac Books Pro models tend to overheat.

This stand can handle the weight of both machines, with the latter coming in at over 4lbs, along with the weight of my hands leaning on it, and there was no indication of it wanting to sag or sink in any way. It will stay put at whatever angle or height you choose. At least it did for me.

There is about an inch to two inches of overhang on either side with larger computers, but it's not much, and both computers felt stable.

Overall, I would say it's a very good, and high-quality laptop stand. However, it is a bit smaller than I expected.

text_fidelity_a:
Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation) The Flip is a pint-sized camcorder with a surprising feature set given its compactness. Though is it not a full-featured camcorder and I would not recommend it for serious recording (special events or production material), it is excellent for on-the-go shots and for spontaneous recording when opportunities present themselves.

The Flip is small - a little smaller than an ice cream sandwich. It may be little, but there's tremendous convenience in being able to drop your camcorder in your shirt pocket or your purse and have it at the ready. This compact size holds everything you need to start recording - batteries, flash RAM and all. Without tapes or DVD media on which to record, there's little reason for this device to be any bigger.

It is a solid little thing and feels durable. That doesn't mean it would do well if dropped or stepped on, but it likely will be ok if jostled a little.

Recording is simple. No, I should be more clear - recording with the Flip is trivial. There is no real science to using it: turn it on, point and press record. Press the record button again to stop recording. Even technological novices, or people afraid of electronics will have no trouble using the Flip to record. Playing back is equally simple - once the recording is finished, press the Play button.

There are + and - buttons, used for Zoom. The Flip doesn't have a particularly capable zoom, so shooting from a distance will not yield especially great results.

I tested this camcorder in my basement on a bright, sunny day, and I wandered about recording and chattering to myself. When I played back what I had recorded, I made a pleasant discovery - it does some light balancing and deals with changes in light levels so that the video is still clear. The sound is also good, better than I expected. When I walked down a dark hallway and into an unlit room, it had tried very hard to accommodate for the lack of light but it was unable to completely overcome the darkness. As there is no light on the camcorder to come on when it is dark, this is understandable, but it did surprisingly well in spite of that.

I attached the Flip to my computer to pull the video to my hard drive. FlipShare installed itself and started up, seeing the video I had made. It allowed me to pull it over and even gave me the option to delete it from the camera. Once finished, I was able to play the video through FlipShare. Instead, I decided to hunt it down and use a different application to play it.

I found the file and tried to open it with Windows Media Player. I got audio, but not video. When I switched to QuickTime, my video came up and filled my screen. This is the point at which I made an unfortunate discovery. Every minute move I had made while recording was now plainly obvious, as there is no anti-jitter built into the device.

The video, on a 1440x900 resolution screen, looked clear. It records at 1280x720, which is not that much smaller, so I was a little surprised. I would have expected a little pixelation, but this actually was not an issue.

There are few settings that can be adjusted on the Flip - language, date, time and recording light.

The Flip is a nice camcorder that provides tremendous convenience and fun. It is very easy to use and very compact. It is important to remember that it has some limitations which make it a less-than-ideal choice for more serious application, but if those limitations are not an issue for you then the Flip is a fun and affordable way to capture things on video.
text_fidelity_b: Flip UltraHD Video Camera - Black, 8 GB, 2 Hours (2nd Generation)

RALENO 2 Packs LED Video Light and 75inches Stand Lighting Kit, CRI 95+ Photography Lighting with 8000mAh Built-in Battery & LCD Display, Studio Lights for TikTok, YouTube, Live Streaming, Videography I ordered the 'RALENO LED Video Lighting Kits With 75inch Light Stand, 1 Durable Handbag And 2-Pack 384 LED Soft Video Light, Built-in Lithium Battery 3200K-6500K Video Lighting Kits For YouTube Photography Shooting' for review and would like to share some of my thoughts.

I ordered this kit to add more lighting options to my photography gear. My first impressions were that this kit is pretty complete in the sense that you get two lights with A/C power cords, stands for both lights, two shoe mounts and a decent carry case. With that said, I was not so impressed with overall quality of all included items. However, for all that you get in this kit, I am still quite impressed. Although this kit isn't of the best build quality it most definitely has great value with all that is included. The lights themselves are smaller than I had expected and the highest brightness setting isn't as bright as I hoped, yet it still has a place, and has come in handy many times to ad a bit more lighting to some of my projects.

I love that it includes the soft case and that the lights themselves have screens on the back that will actually show the color temperatures as well as the brightness level. I have more expensive lights that just have knobs on the back to adjust these settings with no easy way to know what color temperature you are at. This in-of-itself is a huge bonus as far as I am concerned. With this set I an easily select the exact color temp for each light to match. The stands are pretty basic. They are lightweight and easy to set up and take down. I am not so impressed with the quality of the Hot Shoe adapters as they are hard to solidly tighten the angle down without feeling like I am going to break the plastic knobs. They do function however, and I do appreciate that they included these, otherwise you would not be able to adjust the angle of the lights. The soft carrying case is decent and does have some padding if you don't throw out the included foam inserts.

Overall I find this kit to be effective, and have found that even though I may criticize many aspects of it, I do find myself using it quite often because of how convenient and easy to use and set up. There is most definitely value to this kit and I think that it would make a great lighting starter kit as well as a kit to ad more lighting options to your current lights. I hope that this was helpful.
text_fidelity_b: RALENO 2 Packs LED Video Light and 75inches Stand Lighting Kit, CRI 95+ Photography Lighting with 8000mAh Built-in Battery & LCD Display, Studio Lights for TikTok, YouTube, Live Streaming, Videography

text_fidelity_a:
Kensington Ergonomic Vertical Wireless Mouse (K75575WW), Grey/Black Note: There are multiple products attached to this listing. I am specifically reviewing the vertical mouse.

I have used a variety of trackballs, mice, writing tablets and more in my search for the most comfortable pointing device. My weapon of choice has been a higher-end trackball for the last couple of years, and I have a relatively cheap vertical mouse I use on occasion when I need to use that trackball on another system. I've used Kensington trackballs in the past and have had good experiences with them, so I was optimistic about this vertical mouse. So far, it has not disappointed me.

I have the hands of a gorilla so finding a mouse, trackball or any other pointing device usually requires some searching. What fits my hand is often too big for others and what I find too small is usually just right for everyone else. This vertical mouse seems to hit the sweet spot - it's comfortable in my hand and quite usable but it is also good for people with smaller hands. I will say that it is still slightly on the small side for me, and when I use it my pinky finger rests on the desk at the base of this mouse, but it is not uncomfortable and is a step up from others I have used.

In terms of the contour and fit, it is arguably one of the most comfortable vertical mice I have used. My thumb, index and middle fingers rest properly on it and I have no trouble controlling the mouse at all. I do not need to stretch to reach the buttons, but also I do not need to scrunch my hand either. It's a good balance.

Operation is smooth and easy. It is very responsive, it is not loud when the buttons are clicked, and it has a reasonable amount of range.

Considering the cost, it is as close to perfect as I have used. That said, there are a couple of things I would change if I had the opportunity to do so, though the cost would increase. First, I would add the ability to connect via Bluetooth and provide for switching between two connected systems. I have that ability with other peripherals and I like it, though it's a convenience feature. Second, I would add the ability to recharge it instead of replacing batteries. This is a double-edged sword, though - the difference between being up and running with replaceable batteries and rechargeable can be the difference between a minute and a couple of hours.

Because of the nature of vertical mice, it is not switchable between right and left hands. This is very much a right-handed mouse. If you are left-handed, you can use this mouse but it will be very awkward.

One odd thing occurred when I set it up under Windows 10. When I plugged in the receiver it reported it as a wireless keyboard. However, operation has been fine so this is a weird cosmetic issue and I assume that it is because it uses a common receiver.

I like this mouse and am pleased with it. It isn't absolutely perfect and there are some ways in which it could be improved, but to do so would increase the cost appreciably. At the price point, this is one of the best vertical mice I have used.
text_fidelity_b: Kensington Ergonomic Vertical Wireless Mouse (K75575WW), Grey/Black

Amazon Basics Wireless Keyboard with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY) This AMAZON BASICS WIRELESS KEYBOARD (with Touchpad for Smart TV - US Layout (QWERTY)) has the easiest setup I’ve ever encountered for a wireless device. You insert 2 AAA batteries (included) into the keyboard, plug the USB radio receiver into a USB port on your Smart TV, and you’re instantly connected. If for some reason you aren’t automatically connected, you just hit Esc-K to connect.

The keyboard works with my Samsung QLED Q7F Smart TV. Not all of the function keys work with every screen--for example, the keyboard’s “Mute” button does NOT mute the TV--but that’s normal for generic controllers like this one that are intended to work with many different wireless devices.

The keyboard does everything that my Samsung remote does (for example, switches between apps, sources, calls up the TV settings menu), although it takes a bit of experimentation to learn how to use it. The direction keys near the touchscreen allow you to navigate the TV screen and everything else. If you go to the TV’s Internet area, the touchscreen activates and you see a big arrow cursor that works like a mouse.

The keyboard does the one thing that I really wanted. It has a Search button that allows me to search for TV shows, movies, etc. by typing on the keyboard, instead of by navigating around letter-by-letter on an onscreen letterpad. The keyboard does NOT work when I’m using Roku for searches, but that’s normal because the keyboard is designed to connect directly to a Smart TV (not to the TV’s connected accessories).

The keyboard does feel cheap, and I wouldn't want to use it as a computer keyboard. However, it's fine for my occasional use as a Smart TV keyboard.

NOTE: The wireless adapter is stored at the upper left of the box, inside the folded cardboard. The batteries are on the right.

Lenovo IdeaCentre 3 Desktop Tower, AMD Athlon Silver 3050U, AMD Radeon Graphics, 4GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, HDMI, Windows 10 You may know about the announcement from Lenovo a few weeks ago that going forward the company will be certifying all their ThinkPad and Thinkstation workstations for Linux. This computer is an IdeaCentre, not a ThinkPad or ThinkStation, and it comes preloaded with Windows, but I am a Linux user and I wanted to see if it will run Linux.

First things first: If you're looking for a gaming computer or something to handle graphics-intensive programs, this isn't it. It doesn't have a screaming fast processor, although it is a capable one. The onboard AMD Raven graphics module is pretty capable (I tried it out on a big display), but this model has no expansion slot for a video or audio card or any other such upgrades.

It does have a bay for a big 3.5 inch HDD with SATA connectors. And it comes with a 256GB SSD already installed on the motherboard. It also comes with 4GB RAM (and a second slot to add more), and a wired keyboard and mouse and the power supply. It has four USB 2.0 ports in the back, and two 2.0 and two 3.0 (gen 1) USB ports in the front. Also on the front are a card reader slot, the optical drive, mic and headset connection ports, and the power button. The back also has an HDMI port, VGA-out port, and and ethernet port.

It's about the size of an ITX mini tower form factor box, which is a little larger than a big dictionary. It stands upright, so the footprint is pretty small. And it's lightweight compared to a big desktop box.

I didn't even complete the first boot into Windows before attempting a Linux install. Tapping F2 on boot will get you into a graphical menu for picking your boot device, and F12 will get you into a deeper menu for selecting boot order and into the BIOS.

My favorite distro is Debian, so I thought I'd take a shot at installing it. It was a no-go. It didn't have the drivers for the onboard Atheros wifi card, and apparently a few other things. I actually pulled the wifi card off the motherboard and substituted a dongle and gave it a second try. I got Debian installed, but the machine still froze on boot without ever getting into the desktop environment.

So I tried installing Ubuntu, which, along with Red Hat, was specifically mentioned as now being supported by Lenovo. Success. Installation went smoothly. I was still using the dongle for wifi, so I shut down the machine and reinstalled the inboard card. Again, success. Wifi operated right away.

The couple of minor -- emphasizing minor -- things I don't like is that an inboard white LED glows continually when the power supply is plugged in, and as far as I can tell there's no way to turn it off.

Bottom line here is I think it's a good machine for general use. It's pretty capable, but be aware of its limitations so you won't be disappointed.
text_fidelity_b: Lenovo IdeaCentre 3 Desktop Tower, AMD Athlon Silver 3050U, AMD Radeon Graphics, 4GB DDR4, 256GB SSD, Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, HDMI, Windows 10

XSKN Mac OS X Shortcut Silicone US and EU Common Version Keyboard Skin Cover for 2015 and Before 2015 Released MacBook Air Pro 13 15 17 Inch A1278 A1286 A1297 A1342 A1369 A1398 A1425 A1466 A1502 A1314 I used to be able to type 140 words per minute when I was a typographer. The key to speeds like that is not looking at the keyboard, ever. When I received this keyboard skin (in return for my honest review) and put it on my MacBook Pro 15" Retina, I realized why my typing speed has slowed down so much. It's because I always seem to be looking at the keyboard! And having this skin on made me have to unlearn this bad behavior. Now I'm trying to look at it only when I can't remember a keyboard shortcut and need to refer to the key tops for instructions. This is like mini flashcards, a proven learning tool.

Once I got used to how different it is not to be looking at the keyboard all the time, I'm now getting used to the slightly different feel of typing on the skin. It's really a subtle difference. The skin fits exceptionally well, and it's great to know I'm not getting dust and dog hair floating into the keys; also, I don't have to worry quite so much about spilling coffee into the keyboard. I'm also bad about being heavy-handed enough to literally wear the type off the keys, so I know this will protect my laptop from that.

Of course, some keystroke combinations are already second nature to me: Cmd-C, Cmd-V, Cmd-S. But I forget most of the others, so this particular skin is great for me to finish learning the shortcuts. But now, what I really, really, really want, is skins for Serif's award-winning Affinity Designer (Illustrator competitor) and their new Affinity Photo (Photoshop competitor). Please, Lifepersuit, give us skins for these!

One thing to be aware of: Look at the video review elsewhere by the guy who keeps these skins in their package to use as quick-learning guides. I didn't realize it when I receive my skin in a clamshell package that I didn't have to cut the package apart to get the skin out. But—duh!—the package has a tabbed perforation on the back that pulls open easily and can be pressed closed again. So I could have taken my skin out, then if I wanted to use a different skin, I could have stored the skin back in its original package. The package has a hanging hole, so it can be hung on a hook. I wish I hadn't screwed up my original package by cutting it open!

text_fidelity_a:
Monocular High Power Spotting Scope - Baronage 12X42 High Definition Telescope with Smartphone Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter for Adults Bird Watching Camping Travelling. This BARONAGE MONOCULAR TELESCOPE (12X42 High Power BAK4 Prism, with Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter) delivers a lot of bang for the bucks (it costs about $30 on Amazon). It’s pocket-sized (about 6” long, 4” wide), provides good magnification, and comes with both a mini-tripod and a smartphone mount.

The magnification is quite good. The little telescope is great for hand-held viewing of nearby objects of interest. The focus wheel works smoothly, and it is positioned to be very easy to use.

You’ll probably want to use a tripod for taking smartphone photos (though I took some decent photos without one). The photos are pretty good, even if all you do is point, focus (looking at the smartphone display), and shoot. (You won’t be taking prize-winning nature photos with this monocular telescope, but the photos are fine for documenting a trip or other interesting sightings.)

In the attached photos, the tree closeup shows the tree seen in the top center of the second photo (which was taken from the same spot with the smartphone camera alone). The tree closeup appears more sharply focused in my camera gallery than it does here on Amazon; some of the detail was dropped during Amazon's processing.

MOUNTING NOTES: The telescope doesn’t come with instructions for assembling the smartphone mount, or for attaching the telescope to the tripod (see the product page for these). Note that the little projection on the telescope (actually a loop for attaching a lanyard) can be unscrewed to reveal a threaded hole for attaching the tripod.

Also, note that the smartphone mount uses a threaded piece (a round cap with a threaded hole) that screws onto the flat positioning bar that allows you to adjust the position of your smartphone and its camera lens. It’s easy to overlook the cap’s fine threads. The round cap piece fits over the viewer end of the telescope to hold the smartphone clamped in the mount’s pull-out jaws. The mount worked fine with my Samsung Galaxy S7 Edge, and I didn’t even have to take the phone out of its Otterbox Symmetry case.
text_fidelity_b: Monocular High Power Spotting Scope - Baronage 12X42 High Definition Telescope with Smartphone Tripod and Phone Mount Adapter for Adults Bird Watching Camping Travelling.

Fellowes I-Spire Series Laptop Lift/Stand, White/Gray (9311201) Before this stand, I used another Fellowes one for my laptop at home, and it proved its worth--for a while. However, with my new desk setup, I needed something which I could use while changing the height and angle of my laptop screen in a way the old stand simply couldn't. I have a Unicomp keyboard and Logitech mouse which I prefer using, and my "home" laptop needed a better stand.
Enter this Lift.

I've seen many angled laptop stands, and that's what I had in mind when I wanted to switch my old one out. Plus, my old one was better suited for the monitor at work, so I wanted to take that when I had the chance. Finally, I had the opportunity to get an angled one, so I jumped on it.

I'm not using this stand with my laptop by itself. I'm using it as a supplemental to "lift" it up with my home desktop setup being my keyboard and mouse. For that, the stand works marvelously. The angle and height are just about right; I no longer have to arch my neck uncomfortably forward. Plus, I can take my old stand to work and finally have proper posture there too.
I can't see using this by itself. My hands would quickly become painfully uncomfortable. Heck, I can't stand using keyboards with their built-in mini stands. I honestly don't know why they're there; the angle cramps my wrists very fast.

So for my use, I think the stand is great. There's even some empty real estate near the back to put things under, and it seems sturdy enough overall. It's currently holding my Toshiba 17" Windows PC, which is snugly fit.

ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In Ok, I have to admit I'm pretty impressed with this little camera. At first I thought I had to use the Haven subscription, especially after reading the reviews here which said it is necessary. I was kind of bummed about that at first but it turns out this is really useful even without! Sure, being able to record videos and store them in the cloud require a subscription as well as many of the advanced features, but you can still "arm" the camera to snap a photo and alert your phone when it detects motion, which it does splendidly even without a sub. The way I currently use it, it alerts my phone and I can then go to the live view and see and even interact with who is there (talk feature is really cool!).
On top of that, I set ours up with Amazon's Alexa voice service and it is EXTREMELY COOL! I think the speaker seems a bit louder than an Echo Dot, which surprised me. I'm mounting ours by the front porch so we can see people come to the door and interact with them, but we can also use it to play music via Amazon's Alexa when just sitting on the porch drinking coffee. That's an amazing perk that I wasn't expecting before we got it!
I do wish you could combine it with device music groups in Alexa (so I could say, for example, play this song on the everywhere group and it will play inside on our Echo and out on the porch with the Ecobee), but sadly only echo devices can be grouped. That's OK, I knew that before getting this as other devices in our home can't be grouped either (Facebook Portal or Kindles, for example).
If you want to spring for the subscription service, there's a TON of goodies and advanced features beyond even the cloud storage things. But even without that, the live view and photo motion alerts combined with the voice assistant / Alexa integration makes it worth it even just for the hardware alone!
text_fidelity_b: ecobee SmartCamera – Indoor WiFi Security Camera, Smart Home Security System, 1080p HD 180 Degree FOV, Night Vision, 2-Way Audio, Works with Apple HomeKit, Alexa Built In

Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue Unboxing: Wouldn't usually make a section of this, but every once in a while a product makes it a pleasure. Especially a weird one like this. It's like unboxing a little UFO. It starts out in something like a hat box with a couple sticky tabs of tape to remove. Wish they could have found a better closure method, but the box is nice. Inside that you're immediately presented with the odd looking earbuds and a starter guide (also round) that has you immediately trying them on and fitting the best sleeve size for in your ear. There are no extra sleeves obviously apparent, so time to dig deeper. Next up is the UFO. A large earbud like this needs a large charging case. This one is round and unzips like some of the nicer headphone cases, but it's also a hard case with lights and buttons. Nothing inside but a charging dock. Under it is a secret compartment (made less secret by the thumb holes for easy removal). At the bottom of the hat box we have our missing sleeves and a charging cord.

Even with a diagram, putting these on was confusing and took four tries. Once they're on though, they are quite comfortable, and I think I'll learn to put them on after a few more tries.

Back to the book, and ugh! now they're telling me to put them in the charging case to pair. But I just finally got them on! &*^@#!

Ok, after getting things paired and back on, I'm able to put them through some testing. I'm not really an audiophile, but I've tried a lot of earbuds. Comfort is good. They don't rely on being stuck in your ear to hold themselves up, so there isn't a high stress point that's going to get sore first. They sound good. Better than most, but not the best I've heard. The control button is on the back of your ear, and I find it awkward and unreliable. Noise cancellation is solid, but like every other one I've tried, it is hard to tell sometimes because it scales with volume. Turning them on in a noisy room doesn't result in a quiet room, but turning up what you are listening to will result in noise other than what you are listening to disappearing quite a lot. There is a passthrough mode if you need to hear what's going on around you, but it doesn't sound very nice.

I like that it's USB-C. No more having to turn the cord over three times to figure out which end is up, and much faster charging. The case has three lights to show you charge progress for the case Each one represents enough charge for one full use of the earbuds. There's also a light on the top to tell you whether the earbuds are charged yet.

It's a solid product. Not my top favorite, but definitely innovative and a competitive offering.
text_fidelity_b: Shure AONIC 215 Wired Sound Isolating Earbuds, Clear Sound, Single Driver, Secure In-Ear Fit, Detachable Cable, Durable Quality, Compatible with Apple & Android Devices - Blue

text_fidelity_a:
Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Premium Noise Canceling Overhead Headphones with Mic for Phone-Call and Alexa Voice Control, Midnight Blue WH1000XM4 I've heard a lot of wonderful things about the Sony noise cancelling sets like these, and let me tell you: it isn't just hype. The sound quality is excellent, and the noise cancelling is eerily amazing. I put it on my wife and kids with the noise cancelling off and then turned it on to demonstrate, and you can see each them suddenly smile like "whoa". Like my Sony studio headphones I use professionally for work, the actual fidelity of the sound it reproduces is excellent, and the microphone for calls is excellent despite being up by my ears and so far from my mouth (other bluetooth headphones I've tried were good for music only, the mic being up by my ears wasn't good enough to isolate my voice from ambient sound, but this definitely does a great job).
The app gives a ton of control beyond what I expected to really customize the experience. For example, I have mine set to auto-pause if the headphones are removed, and to turn off noise cancelling when it detects me speaking to someone, and then resume playback when the headphones are removed/replaced. These features are all customizable, as well as many more. But you need the app. And this is where the cons come in:
1) You really need the app to get the most out of this. I was thinking about pairing this with my desktop and/or TV, but without the app you have far less control, and to be honest I couldn't even get it to pair with my phone using just Bluetooth alone. There seems to be a way according to the instructions, but I couldn't figure it out without using the app installed.
2) For a set that costs this much, I'm surprised at how scuffed up it got after one fall from about 3 feet next to my car. Including pictures. This happened the day I got it. I'm not sure if there's anything that can be done about that, pavement is hard to recover from if anything is dropped, but it's something to keep in mind if you're spending this much money on a gadget. My studio headphones have been roughed around for years and held up fine.

All in all, I'd give it 5 stars if it weren't so reliant on the app to get the features going and/or more resilient to being dropped. Feels like I should deduct one for that. But as far as features and sound quality go, this is a solid 5 out of 5.
text_fidelity_b: Sony WH-1000XM4 Wireless Premium Noise Canceling Overhead Headphones with Mic for Phone-Call and Alexa Voice Control, Midnight Blue WH1000XM4

text_fidelity_a:
D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655) We are very satisfied with the two DIR-655s that we have (at two sites). They hold up well and cause no problems. They're fast and stable; they run cool and basically require little or no attention.

Two router features that deserve much more discussion than they usually get are the unit's firewall (if any) and its Quality-of-Service (QoS) engine (if any).

o The firewall keeps external probes and hack-attempts out of your network. You'd be amazed how many probes a home or business broadband connection gets every hour from places like China, Eastern Europe and the Middle East. They're looking for ways in so they can infect your machines and steal your information. A router with a good firewall implemented in its firmware is increasingly essential. Firewalls let internal users establish connections with remote machines, not the other way around. And the DIR-655's firewall is excellent, a stateful-packet-inspection implementation that is truly industrial-class. Frankly, I didn't know this when I bought my first unit but was delighted to discover it once I brought it home. Good stuff. And, it's compatible with my company's virtual-private-network (VPN) approaches, which can be a real problem for firewalls to accommodate. My company has used two VPN approaches in the time I've had our DIR-655s, and there have been no issues.

o A good QoS engine prioritizes time-critical Internet traffic such as voice-over-Internet (VoIP). I did not fully appreciate this until we pulled the plug on our landline and implemented "roll-your-own VoIP", saving 90% off our monthly phone costs (see [...] for details). Only a router with good QoS capabilities will allow phone calls to be clear, crisp and smooth in the face of other Internet traffic. And the DIR-655 turns out to have a very good QoS engine. It automatically prioritizes the standard VoIP ports so our phone calls sound as good as a landline even with two teenagers streaming video, cruising Facebook, listening to Pandora, Skyping and FaceTime-ing, etc. Unfortunately, the marketplace is not yet fully aware of the benefits of a good QoS engine in routers, so it's not a given. Even Apple's well-regarded and excellent Time Capsule and Airport/Airport Extreme routers don't have it, for example. But DIR-655 does.

The only issue we've ever experienced with the DIR-655s in our years of usage was once when a cell phone got into a conniption loop that had it disassociate and reassociate with the router over and over and over again, many times per minute. This caused the router to bog down and reboot itself (and who could blame it). The DIR-655's informative logs helped me diagnose what was going on. Eventually the phone got straightened out, and the problem went away.

UPDATE: I can no longer recommend this router. The latest firmware is abysmal and ruins what was formerly a good product.
text_fidelity_b: D-Link Wireless N300 Mbps Extreme-N Gigabit Router (DIR-655)

text_fidelity_a:
Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case Bought this for the 750 because it didn't come with a case. A similar (smaller) case came with my 360 and I didn't think this purchase through. After using it and comparing the other cases out there, I would buy a different case.

This slipcase for the 750 fits tight. That's good. The Nuvi won't slip out. But because the 750's on/off switch is now a slider on the top left corner, if you slide it into the case naturally (unit in your right hand, case in your left) the switch rubs against the case. When you pull the unit out, it "automatically" turns on. Thus if you were to pull the unit out partially then push it back in, you could turn it on and not know it.

The solution is to invert the Nuvi so its switch will be at the open end of the case after it's in the case. That way you can see the switch's on/off position and verify it's not on.

More practical issues:

Pros:

- Nicely made: very high quality

- Very compact

- Adequate protection against rattling inside a glove compartment or briefcase

- Good basic case

Cons:

- It can accidentally turn the unit on

- It's black: can't find it easily in the dark buried at the bottom of my shoulder bag when traveling. Experienced this with the 360's case. And if it falls on the floor of a rental car at night, good luck trying to find it. Wish it came in natural leather color.

- Offers no protection while hand holding the unit while walking

The [[ASIN:B0012MI7N2 Garmin Nuvi 800 Series Carrying Case]] case is a wallet style that flips open to reveal the screen. It stays on the unit during use and offers some protection if you dropped your Nuvi on the sidewalk while walking. Downside with that unit appears to be that the cover flap does not latch, allowing the case to flip open in a briefcase and the screen to be scratched by other junk. And it's also black and can get lost on a car floor.

Another alternate is one of the many zippered semi-rigid or neoprene cases.
text_fidelity_b: Garmin 4.3-Inch Carrying Case

text_fidelity_a:
MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP THINGS YOU'LL NEED THAT ARE NOT INCLUDED:
----------------------------------------------------------
1. Your own micro SD card, up to 2tb.
2. A power adapter that has a usb-c port. The Qubii will be plugged into this adapter.
3. A usb-c to usb-c cable. To connect from the Qubii to the usb-c port of your Android phone.
4. A usb-c to Apple lightning if you'll be using an iPhone.

SOME NOTEWORTHY INFO:
---------------------------------
* This is a good idea, now that Google Photos is no longer unlimited.
* It basically backs-up every folder that has an image. There doesn't seem to be a way to choose which folders you want it to back-up. I only need my main camera folder to get backed-up, but oh well, backing up too much is better than too little.
* Once you disconnect from power adapter, you can use the Qubii as OTG storage. You'll need to turn on OTG storage in your system settings. If you have a case on your phone, you'll probably never bother to use it as OTG because you'll need to remove the case.
* Every time you want to transfer files to your PC, NAS, etc., you'll need to remove the micro sd card if your pc doesn't have a usb-c port. My PC does not, so I use a usb to usb-c adapter. This eliminates the hassle of having to take out micro sd cards, dealing with card readers, etc.
* After you transfer everything safely to your pc, if you delete the files on the micro SD card to clear space, the Qubii still maintains its count. So even if these files are still on your phone, it will not re-download them again.

In conclusion, how accurate and precise this system is remains to be seen. So far, it has backed up everything I need it to. I know people complain of missing files, not everything getting backed-up, etc. Most of these complaints revolves around people using iPhones. But we'll see, time will tell. As of now, this is 5-Stars!
text_fidelity_b: MAKTAR Qubii Duo USB-C Flash Drive(White Without microSD), Auto Backup While Charging, MFi Certified Compatible with iPhone/iPad/Android, Photo Storage/Stick with File Organizer APP

text_fidelity_a:
Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White Black Friday sales have brought the Echo Dot to under $30, and that is how I am now buying my second one.

So yes, often times you do need to formulate your requests in a certain way (for instance, try asking Alexa how much time it will take to go to work... I gave up on this...) and enunciate them more clearly if you missed, but in general, this technology is just amazing.
Sometimes I even ask Alexa for information I don't need, just for fun.

I like that they named it Alexa. That's so much better than "Okay Google." It feels like a real person. Who in hell at Google thought it's a good idea to force users to use their company name, and thus remind them that their huge creepy analytics private data gathering network is behind it?

Possible improvements:
* Bring back the matte finish from 1st gen. I shouldn't have to pay more to not have it shiny...
* Listen to the word "stop" when the alarm is ringing. Currently you need to wait until it's not ringing and then say "Alexa, stop."
* Add confirmation and modification prompts to "Add a new event to the calendar." Currently if she misunderstood one word, you have to start all over again.
* Alexa bluntly tells you that she cannot tell you about the events in your calendar on a specific date... C'mon guys...
* Implement the word "Repeat": sometimes you didn't hear or didn't catch the information you were looking for, and currently you have to formulate your request again
* Only gives info about the last Amazon order. She can retrieve more order but you have to be very specific about what they contain.
* I wish Alexa could Google more stuff.
* Choose your own wake up word

I never use Siri on my iPhone, but for some reason it feels very natural to use Alexa, maybe because the device is more "fixed" whereas my phone could be in a backpack, in the other room...

The Killer App is MUSIC. We have an Echo Dot in the bedroom, and my wife just loves to ask Alexa for tunes. We have it linked to Spotify.

Also, I am a software engineer, and I have added some custom features through my own skills. I wish somebody came up with something simple to add your own skills, because this is really useful. For instance, the bus comes in front of my house at the most random times, so I developed a skill that tells me in how many minutes the next buses will come. So much faster than having to check a website on my phone!
text_fidelity_b: Echo Dot (2nd Generation) - Smart speaker with Alexa - White

FLAGTOP 7 in 1 USB C Hub for Universal Devices, Support 4K HDMI/PD 3.0 / USB 3.0 / 2USB 2.0 / SD/Micro SD/TF, USB Type C Dongle Hub (02A) I have a 2017 MacBook Pro with 4 Thunderbolt/USB C ports. Of course almost every peripheral I use is USB 2.0/3.0, so I have adapters everywhere and can never find one when I need it, or don’t have enough ports to plug in everything I want to use.

So this USB C Hub from Flagtop is super handy to have around. I use it to connect a second monitor (HDMI port), an external mouse/keyboard (USB 2.0 ports), and the power cable (USB C port).

I like that the USB 2.0/USB 3.0 ports have a little space between each one. This makes them usable even if you have a thick thumb drive or cable plugged in.

I had to have the ports on my laptop replaced because they loosened up over time, so I like that I can reduce wear on the new ports by unplugging the hub to disconnect everything.

SZILBZ Keyboard Case An attractive case -- I tested the Rose Gold version -- nicely made with no obvious flaws. I've been trying various types of external keyboards as I like to use my iPad on trips and blog as I go. Having a full keyboard makes life a lot easier.

This is the first integrated case/keyboard I've tried, and so far, I like it. It's easy to set up -- charge it (a cable is provided), pop in the iPad, turn on, pair, and you're set to go.

The backlight is fully adjustable - brightness as well as color. That's a nice touch. Battery life seems to be excellent -- I've used it 2-3 hours every day for the past 10 days, and it's still going strong and it still hasn't indicated I need to recharge it. The keyboard size is a bit smaller than my MacBook Air laptop, but after a few minutes, I got used to the slightly tighter quarters and had no issues at all. Getting it into the case is easy; getting it out of the case takes a little more effort. When I take it along on my trips, I'll leave it in the case for the duration.

My only complaint is that it's quite heavy but given the battery capacity, that's probably not too surprising. So the trade-off is a slightly heavier case with LONG battery life, or a keyboard-only solution with much shorter battery life. I think in the end, I'll appreciate the longer battery life and fully integrated case/keyboard.

I'll continue to use this over the next few months, and plan to take it on my next couple of trips. If all goes well, it will come along on a 131-day world cruise early next year.
text_fidelity_b: SZILBZ Keyboard Case

Hyperion GPS Dash Cam with 4K Video Display and 120° Wide Angle View, Rechargeable with Built-in Mic, Lane Divergence and Collision Alerts The Hyperion auto dash camera is a decent dash cam for the money. It is easy to install and the suction cup holder is very secure. You can choose three different video resolutions; 1296P, 1080P, or 720P. The higher the resolution the shorter the recording duration before the video starts loop recording. You can increase memory by inserting a higher capacity memory card, it comes with a 16GB memory card installed already and it can take a 32GB or up to a 64GB memory card. The recording modes/video files are, Crash detected, Loop-recording, Parking and Photo. You can plug your camera to you computer with the supplied cable to transfer the videos or you can pop out the memory card and put it in a card reader on your computer to transfer the videos. You can also update the camera the same way, if there is an update to the camera.

The camera has other functions as well, it has Advanced Driver Assistance Systems (ADAS), Lane Departure Warning System (LDWS), Front Collision Warning System, Front Vehicle Departure Warning. They seem to work, but I wouldn't rely on it. It just give beeping tones and sometimes it seems random whey they go off, also if you pass other drivers or vice versa it beeps as well. The good thing is in the menu settings, you can disable the alarms and it doesn't affect the camera recording.

Installation is pretty simple, it comes with a long power cord that can be easily concealed under the trim. The only thing that might be a problem is you need to plug it into the cigarette lighter, so if you don't have another lighter plug outlet, you would have to unplug the camera to for example plug in a cellphone charger. The camera does have a rechargeable battery built in so it can run on battery power for a while, but you have to have the camera plugged in for a while to charge the battery first.

Overall, this is a nice camera and I am very happy with it.
